questions.question: If you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test, what happens?

options.text: You fail only that exercise.
You lose extra points.
You automatically fail the entire test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire test.
questions.explanation: You must face the vehicle and use three points of contact when exiting. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you automatically fail the test.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, who decides whether to proceed?

options.text: The driver.
A control device.
The vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic control devices. The driver alone decides whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: If a student drops something while approaching a school bus, what should they do?

options.text: Pick it up themselves.
Have another student pick it up.
Ask the driver to pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick it up.
questions.explanation: If a student bends down to pick something up, the driver cannot see them. This is dangerous. Instead, students should move to safety, get the driver's attention, and let the driver retrieve the item.

questions.question: How is student safety best maintained in an emergency?

options.text: Keep students on the bus.
Let some students leave the bus.
Let all students leave and spread out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep students on the bus.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safest and easiest to control if they stay on the bus. Keep them on the bus as long as there is no immediate danger.

questions.question: When dropping off students at school, what should the driver do?

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Leave the key in the ignition.
Read a book while students leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine when unloading students. Remove the key if you leave the driver's seat. You must watch the students as they leave.

questions.question: When inspecting the fifth wheel gap before a trip, what should you check?

options.text: That there is a gap between the kingpin and locking jaws.
That the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
That the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Look into the fifth wheel gap and make sure the locking jaws are completely closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: What should you check when inspecting the fifth wheel gap?

options.text: That the locking jaws are open.
That the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
That the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: The locking jaws must be closed around the shank of the kingpin, not the head.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what happens?

options.text: You do not need to know about railroad crossings.
You may be asked to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
You must take the test again on a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be asked to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not have a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would properly cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Not use their mirrors.
Approach slowly and carefully.
Stop on the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver should always slow down and be cautious when approaching bus stops.

questions.question: What is an active railroad crossing?

options.text: A crossing with traffic control devices.
A crossing with no traffic control devices.
A crossing used by at least 10 vehicles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossing with traffic control devices.
questions.explanation: Active crossings have control devices like flashing red lights, bells, and gates. Drivers must follow the instructions of these devices.

questions.question: Who can change bus stops?

options.text: The driver.
Parents.
The school district.

questions.correctAnswerText: The school district.
questions.explanation: The school district sets official bus routes and stops. Drivers cannot change a stop without written permission from a district official.

questions.question: When backing into an alley, what should you do first?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.
questions.explanation: When alley docking, drive past the alley first. Stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle into the parking space in a straight line.

questions.question: What does ABS help you do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Maintain control under slippery conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain control under slippery conditions.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your brakes from locking up on slippery roads. This helps you keep control of your vehicle when braking hard on wet or icy surfaces. Drive and brake the same way in a vehicle with or without ABS.

questions.question: Where should students sit when boarding a bus?

options.text: Sit in the back row first.
Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
Be seated as far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
questions.explanation: Students should use the back row only when the bus is full. Students are safer sitting closer to the front in case of a rear-end collision. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.

questions.question: During testing, how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position?

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during most exercises. This is called a "look." During straight line backing, you may only take one look. During other exercises, you may take up to two looks.

questions.question: What can you NOT see with properly adjusted crossover mirrors?

options.text: The right and left front tires touching the ground.
The area in front of the bus.
The tops of the right and left rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tops of the right and left rear tires.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors should show the entire area in front of the bus from the front bumper to where you can see directly. They should also show the front tires and the area from the front to the service door. They do not show the tops of the rear tires.

questions.question: What maneuver might you be asked to do during a vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Swerve to avoid a hazard.
Parallel park.
Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: The vehicle control skills test includes straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: Attitude.
How quickly you arrive to your destination.
Your general driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your general driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on specific driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior during the on-road test.

questions.question: What should you do when stopped at a railroad crossing in a school bus?

options.text: Prepare to proceed as soon as a train passes.
Ignore signs and signals.
Open the door to listen for approaching trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the door to listen for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: Do not rely only on signals at railroad crossings. Quiet all passengers, open the front door, and look and listen for trains. After a train passes, check for another train from either direction before crossing.

questions.question: Where should students stay during an emergency?

options.text: On the bus
On the side of the road near the bus
In a field away from the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: On the bus
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safer and easier to control on the bus. Only evacuate students if staying on the bus puts them at risk.
